chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'How is the prayer offered over men and women?' He said, 'Men are placed facing the men, and women are behind the men.'
ai.seo_question: How are men and women arranged during the funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the standard spatial arrangement for Salat al-Janazah, where men stand in rows facing the deceased and women stand in rows behind them. This configuration reflects the general principle of gender segregation in congregational prayers within Shia jurisprudence, ensuring modesty while maintaining the communal nature of the funeral rite.
